rules.floor: At each close, floor is 90% of the maximum observed closing account equity, including initial capital. No annual or post-loss reset.
rules.risk_weight: Cushion multiplier times positive equity-minus-floor divided by equity, capped to the 98% investable budget.
rules.defense: Remaining investable weight goes to actual BIL ETF, with a separate 2% zero-interest cash reserve at rebalance.
rules.decision_timing: Compute only at completed closes; each signal executes after one session (base) or two sessions (stress). A later close cannot cancel a queued signal retrospectively.
rules.rebalance_trigger: Risk-weight deviation from the computed target at least one percentage point, or complete risk exit when the floor is breached.
rules.initial_entry: Each ten/five-year account starts with USD10,000 and a known initial floor; initial allocation is decided at the session immediately before the evaluation window.
rules.stress_state: Higher cost and delay alter actual account state and hence future rule outputs. Same feedback law, not artificially held-identical target weights.
rules.numerical_no_trade: If all intended pre-cost dollar changes are at most 1e-6 USD, there is no order and no fixed commission.

disclosures: TIPP-inspired discrete-time ratcheting-floor implementation, not a claim of reproducing the original paper's exact product, data, or returns.
Original publication metadata is verified; publisher full-text access was unavailable.
TQQQ and UPRO have embedded daily leverage; no broker borrowing is used.
A theoretical floor is not guaranteed with discrete trading, opening gaps, fees, and a non-guaranteed bond ETF.
Floor breaches and prolonged low risky exposure are measured, not repaired by new capital or history resets.
The strategy must still pass all existing ten/five-year return, Sharpe, drawdown and SPY gates; the 90% floor is only a mechanism hypothesis.
Recent history was previously examined and cannot be relabeled as an independent holdout.
